Sara — thanks for the redlines and clear questions. We ran a quick triage with legal and infra; high level:
- SCCs: we generally accept the EU Commission SCCs verbatim for hosted flows. For private/VPC deployments we can attach the Commission text or use your annex; legal prefers the Commission text but can accept customer annexes with limited edits.
- Controller/Processor: Redwood proposes controller = NovaMed, processor = Redwood for processing of customer data generated during the pilot. We can add explicit examples in the DPA to reflect patient telemetry.
- Transfer Impact Addendum: we do have a Transfer Impact Addendum template we use for hybrid hosting and on-prem fallbacks. I asked our legal team to draft a tailored annex for the pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal legal (Laura) to prepare a Redwood-proposed DPA annex and mark key differences vs your redline.
2) I’ll consolidate the MSA/order form redlines and circulate a single PDF for signature routing.
3) Call with your legal/procurement on Thursday to walk the annex and SCCs choice — would 3pm CET work?

Attaching internal tracker link and I’ll follow up shortly with our draft annex.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Novamed MSA redlines — quick triage

Laura / Ben — see Sara's attachment (Novamed_MSA_Redlines.docx) and highlights below. Key asks from Novamed: SCCs choice, explicit controller/processor examples, and an addendum for hybrid transfers. They also flagged a KMS requirement for EU keys.

My notes:
- SCCs: customer prefers their annex (comments in section 5). Legal preference is Commission text to avoid negotiation overhead. Recommend offering Commission text and a short mapping table showing deviations if they insist on annex.
- Controller/Processor: Novamed wants language that limits Redwood's processing scope to inference and logging. They want explicit mention that pseudonymisation and telemetry are included. Laura: can we draft clause bullets that enumerate 5 processing activities?
- Transfer Impact Addendum: we should use our TI Addendum template but add a paragraph for private deployment fallbacks and KMS options (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed keys).

Please draft the DPA annex and redline suggestions; I’ll coordinate a customer call Thu 15:00 CET / 9:00 EDT.

Thanks — Karthik

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Internal: Novamed MSA redlines — quick triage

Folks — attached is a working draft: Redwood_DPA_Suggested_Annex_v2.docx. High level comments inline, but summary below:
- Using Commission SCCs as the primary attachment reduces negotiation. I included a short table mapping Novamed's annex items to the Commission clauses (see p.2).
- Controller/Processor clause: drafted 5 bullet processing purposes (inference, logging/monitoring, customer support, security, analytics for service improvement).
- KMS: included BYOK option for EU-only keys with explicit SLA for key rotation and key export restrictions. If customer selects BYOK we require a minimal onboarding fee and an Ops runbook for key provisioning.
- Transfer Impact Addendum: added language for fallback to on-prem and for subprocessor routing. Also included a commitment to provide evidence (SOC2+ list of subprocessors) during procurement.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Suggested_Annex_v2.docx (draft annex)

Quick question for Ben: will the BYOK onboarding fee be part of order form pricing or handled as a Professional Services charge?

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
